sentence: Bladder cancer is cancer that forms in the tissues of the bladder, the organ that stores urine.
note: NCI: cancer that forms in the bladder's tissues; MedlinePlus: bladder cancer.

sentence: Blood in the urine is the most common sign of bladder cancer, according to Macmillan and MedlinePlus.
note: Macmillan symptoms page: blood in pee is the most common sign; MedlinePlus: blood in the urine is the most common warning sign.

sentence: Many people with blood in their urine do not have bladder cancer, but the NHS advises asking for an urgent GP appointment or contacting NHS 111.
note: Macmillan: many do not have bladder cancer; NHS: urgent GP appointment or NHS 111.

sentence: Smoking is the biggest known risk factor for bladder cancer.
note: NHS 111 Wales: smoking is the single biggest risk factor; MedlinePlus: smoking is the largest risk factor.

sentence: Treatment depends on the stage and type of the cancer, and the NHS says surgery is usually offered first, with chemotherapy, radiotherapy or immunotherapy added in some cases.

sentence: Imaging such as a CT urogram may also be used, and abnormal areas can be removed in an operation called TURBT so they can be tested for cancer.

Removing the whole bladder, called cystectomy, is used for higher-risk or muscle-invasive disease, and radiotherapy with chemotherapy is another approach.

sentence: Macmillan says it can start suddenly and may come and go.

sentence: Other symptoms include a burning feeling when passing urine, needing to pass urine more often, rushing to the toilet, difficulty passing urine and a feeling that the bladder has not fully emptied.
note: Macmillan: burning when peeing, needing to pee more often, rushing to the toilet, difficulty peeing, bladder not emptying.

sentence: Pain in the lower tummy or back is less common.
note: Macmillan: pain in the lower tummy or back is less common with bladder cancer.

sentence: Macmillan says these urinary symptoms are usually caused by an infection, an overactive bladder or an enlarged prostate rather than cancer.

sentence: A Bristol NHS urology page explains that chemicals from tobacco are filtered into the urine and sit against the bladder lining.
note: NBT (NHS) page via search summary: tobacco carcinogens are filtered into urine and sit against the bladder lining.

sentence: Estimates of how much smoking contributes vary: NHS 111 Wales says more than a third of cases are caused by it, while Macmillan suggests about half.
note: NHS 111 Wales: more than a third; Macmillan: smoking may cause about 5 in 10 bladder cancers (search summary, page not named).

sentence: The Royal Marsden says heavy, long-term smoking carries the most risk.
note: Royal Marsden page via search summary.

sentence: Exposure to certain chemicals at work is another recognised factor.
note: Search summary of NHS trust pages: workplace chemicals (aromatic amines, aniline dyes) are the next major factor.

sentence: These include aromatic amines and aniline dyes, with jobs in dye production, textiles, rubber, plastics and paint linked to higher risk.
note: Search summary of NHS trust pages listed these chemicals and industries (page-level attribution not certain).

sentence: Cancers linked to these chemicals can take many years to appear, so past exposure still matters.
note: Search summary: can take up to 30 years after exposure to appear.

sentence: NHS pages list being older and being male as other factors.

sentence: Repeated urinary infections and long-term or untreated bladder stones have been linked to a less common type called squamous cell bladder cancer.

sentence: Having a risk factor does not mean a person will develop bladder cancer.

note: Search summary of CRUK: can be awake with local anaesthetic, or asleep under general anaesthetic.

sentence: If cystoscopy shows abnormal areas, an operation called TURBT can remove them so that the tissue can be tested for cancer.
note: Search summaries: TURBT removes abnormal tissue found at cystoscopy so it can be tested.

sentence: For non-muscle-invasive disease, an operation called TURBT removes visible tumours through the urethra.
note: Search summary of NHS treatment page.

sentence: For early disease, a single dose of chemotherapy can be placed directly into the bladder through a catheter after surgery.
note: Search summary of NHS treatment page.

sentence: Treatments such as BCG immunotherapy or mitomycin chemotherapy can also be placed directly into the bladder for non-muscle-invasive disease.
note: PMC12282301 compares intravesical BCG and mitomycin C for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

sentence: A review describes BCG as the standard treatment after surgery for high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease.
note: Search summary: intravesical BCG is the standard treatment for fully resected high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease.

sentence: Removing the whole bladder, called cystectomy, is used for higher-risk or muscle-invasive disease and is major surgery.
note: Search summary of NHS treatment page: cystectomy is major surgery used for higher-risk or muscle-invasive disease.

sentence: Radiotherapy may be used instead of surgery, and is often combined with chemotherapy, which is called chemoradiotherapy.
note: Search summary of NHS treatment page.

sentence: Reviews describe radical cystectomy as the standard option for muscle-invasive bladder cancer, with chemoradiotherapy as a bladder-sparing alternative for some people.
note: PMC5433354 and PMC4779141 via search summary.

sentence: One review notes that no randomised trials have directly compared the two approaches.
note: Search summary: no randomised control trials have yet directly compared radical cystectomy with bladder-preserving chemoradiation.

sentence: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer often comes back after treatment.
note: PMC8571151: NMIBC recurs often; PMC12327299 reports recurrence in a retrospective cohort.

sentence: Reviews describe high rates of recurrence in the first years after treatment, and some tumours can progress.
note: Search summary of PMC8571151 / PMC3999003: high recurrence rates in first 5 years; risk of progression.

sentence: For this reason, follow-up is long-term, and one review describes it as lifelong.
note: PMC8571151 via search summary: recurrence rates require lifetime follow-up.

sentence: Cystoscopy is the standard method of follow-up, often combined with urine tests and imaging of the upper urinary tract.
note: Search summary of PMC8571151: surveillance pairs cystoscopy with urine cytology and upper tract imaging.

sentence: The schedule is usually adapted to the risk category of the tumour.
note: Search summary of PMC8571151: follow-up schedule adapted to predicted EORTC risk.

sentence: Urine-based tests are being studied, but reviews say none has yet replaced cystoscopy in routine practice.
note: Search summary: no urinary biomarker accepted or recommended in routine practice to replace cystoscopy.

sentence: Treatment placed into the bladder can have side effects.
